description: Fixture corpus for editorial regression (AES-P3.1 / SUE-449). Small enough to rerun after every rule or Skill change. Bodies only — no front matter — so a fixture is a fixture and never an article.
rights_policy: All fixtures are synthetic or owner-authored. No third-party article is reproduced. External material appears as reference only. See editorial/RIGHTS-AND-PROVENANCE.md.

fixtures.why: The shape a passing article has: thesis in the first paragraph, synthesis across sources that disagree, numbers rather than adjectives, a stated limit, and a closing that lands a consequence.
The View register: position first, the strongest objection stated at full strength and conceded where it lands, and an explicit condition that would change the author's mind.
anti_patterns_avoided: opinion in the register of neutral research

fixtures.why: The Note register: one observation, the author's judgment kept, well under the 800-word cap. Brevity here is correctness, not thinness.
anti_patterns_avoided: inflating an observation into a report

fixtures.why: Seven calibration cases (SUE-523): the same facts and argument as N-04-translationese, expressed in native Korean discourse order. Cases 1-6 are sentence-level, one failure signature each; case 7 is paragraph-length, reordering sentences relative to each other rather than words within one sentence, since sentence-level cases alone cannot demonstrate discourse order. Every rewrite keeps an explicit subject as an antecedent before dropping it later, restructures rather than swaps scaffolding synonyms, and adds no claim the source does not make. Counterpart to N-04, not a paired regression — see N-04's header for the per-case failure signature and rewrite rationale.
anti_patterns_avoided: English clause order and English-shaped discourse order preserved under correct Korean grammar
scaffolding swapped for a synonym instead of removed
claim strengthened or made proportional beyond what the source states

fixtures.origin: reconstructed from the SUE-417 first end-to-end draft
fixtures.why: The transport path passed and the editorial result failed. This fixture exists so that distinction stays visible.
failure_modes: the generator instruction emitted as the dek and the first body line
one paragraph repeated verbatim
planning notes shipped as content
formulaic sectioning with nothing behind it
a hedge carrying no number
each citing paragraph on one source, in order

fixtures.why: Every citation resolves; none supports the claim beside it. Proves the mechanical layer is insufficient on its own — this is caught by verify-claims, not by a gate.
failure_modes: a source supporting a weaker version of the claim, cited as if it supported the stronger one
a source from a different period and scope, cited as current evidence
a conclusion asserted as confirmed by two citations that establish neither

fixtures.why: Smoother than the golden fixture and factually worse. Every editorial dimension improves; two integrity dimensions fail. The evaluation must report this as a regression, or it is measuring the wrong thing.
failure_modes: a number changed under cover of a style pass (30% → 40%)
a citation dropped from a retained claim
a stated uncertainty softened into a confident claim
a limit inverted into a premise

fixtures.why: Same seven facts and argument as G-04-korean-native, expressed with repeated translationese discourse scaffolding named in voice.md's 'Native Korean, not translated Korean' section — ~라는 점에서 / ~다는 점에서 / ~의 관점에서 / 이러한 맥락에서 / 결국 중요한 것은, abstract noun stacking, subject repetition, and preserved English discourse order. Demonstrates that G-13 fires on genuine repetition of the same scaffold, not on several different ones each used once (see quality-gates.md's G-13 note).
failure_modes: ~라는 점에서 / ~다는 점에서 / ~의 관점에서 stacked as third-party-viewpoint and justification scaffolding (not author self-positioning)
이를 통해 / 이러한 맥락에서 standing in for a direct causal clause
결국 중요한 것은 scaffolding wrapping an abstract noun stack around a hidden verb
mechanical 따라서/한편 glue plus "A는 B를 의미한다" repeated as English-style declarative scaffolding
~에 대한 / ~에 있어 / ~을 통해 nominal stacking preserving English clause order
a subject restated across three consecutive sentences instead of dropped after first mention
English essay discourse order (general claim, self-referential preview, data, conclusion) instead of Korean-shaped sentence order within one paragraph

expected.note: flag-severity only — Korean naturalness is judgement, per voice.md and rubric dimension E-13; this fixture is not expected to hard-fail

fixtures.why: The specific guard against the risk SUE-523's editorial-polish changes create: subject omission, verb-forward rewriting, de-nominalization, and connective removal, each applied past the point voice.md recommends. Deliberately gate-invisible — every defect here is a judgement failure (ambiguous referent, flattened uncertainty, chopped rhythm), not a mechanical one, so no gate in quality-gates.json is expected to fire.
failure_modes: subject dropped between two plausible-but-unresolved antecedents (팀 vs 벤더), realistic rather than a caricature — a careful reader has to stop and work out who acted
stated uncertainty (원인은 확정되지 않았다) flattened into a confident claim one sentence later with no new evidence
hypotactic sentences chopped into clipped, efficient-sounding status-log fragments, against voice.md §5, without being a strawman no polish pass would emit

expected.note: documented as a case no gate should reach — this is what editorial-polish must not become, not a positive example of anything

calibration.question: Does the calibrated editorial contract produce a materially better result than the first end-to-end draft?
calibration.note: Both are news-register pieces on the same subject. The baseline is the SUE-417 smoke draft's failure shape; the calibrated fixture is what the contract now requires. Measured by hard-fail status and gate findings, not by a subjective read.
